lead.tldr: Liquidation cascade accelerated by margin calls across crypto and traditional assets, with $1.7B in Bitcoin long positions wiped out as BTC fell below $81,000 • Fed's hawkish stance and persistent Bitcoin ETF outflows ($2.8B wave) removed institutional bid support, shifting safe-haven flows toward precious metals and cash • Geopolitical tensions and thin Asia liquidity amplified algorithmic selling, with gamma squeeze mechanics adding 2-3% additional downside pressure to the move • Crypto theft losses hit $370M in January, highest in 11 months, signaling elevated security risks amid market volatility and investor desperation

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The crypto market faces a defining moment as Bitcoin plummets amid a $1.7 billion liquidation cascade triggered by margin calls and algorithmic feedback loops. Meanwhile, strategic capital flows continue reshaping the landscape, with major institutional players repositioning across digital assets and traditional finance.

top_signals.title: Krypto Crash: Das steckt hinter der massiven Entwertung von BTC und Co
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin has crashed below $80,000 to around $75,000-$77,000 amid a global liquidation cascade exceeding $2 billion, driven by extreme over-leveraging, macroeconomic headwinds like Fed rate hike expectations, and institutional ETF outflows totaling $6.18 billion since November. This marks Bitcoin's worst weekly drop since the 2022 crypto winter, erasing over $200 billion in market value and breaching key supports like the 200-day SMA, with altcoins suffering similar losses. For institutional investors, the event signals heightened risk from ETF unrealized losses averaging 15%, with average entry at $90,200, potentially amplifying selling pressure, though longer-term horizons may limit capitulation. Whale distributions contrast with some resilient institutional accumulation, positioning the dip as a potential buying opportunity amid oversold conditions indicated by a Fear & Greed Index of 14.

top_signals.title: Abu Dhabi royal bought big stake in Trump family crypto venture
top_signals.source: James Politi, Andrew England, George Steer
top_signals.summary: Investors backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed al-Nahyan invested $500 million into World Liberty Financial, a crypto venture associated with the Trump family.

top_signals.title: Trump family crypto firm sold major stake to UAE investment firm
top_signals.summary: A UAE investment firm acquired a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial, a Trump family crypto company. The investment is reportedly worth $500 million.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin ETF Investors Underwater After $2.8B Outflow Wave
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin ETF investors are facing losses as $2.8 billion has flowed out of the ETFs, causing Bitcoin to fall to a nine-month low of $74,600.

top_signals.title: Crypto Thefts Rise Fourfold Over Year to $370M in January
top_signals.summary: Crypto thefts surged in January, reaching $370 million, the highest monthly amount since February 2025. CertiK reports that phishing scams were the primary cause of these exploits.

top_signals.title: Crypto Losses Hit $370M in January 2026, Highest in 11 Months: CertiK
top_signals.summary: Cryptocurrency losses from exploits and scams reached $370.3 million in January 2026, the highest monthly total in 11 months. This represents a significant increase compared to the same period last year, according to CertiK.
